chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Bird leaves Harlan Leonard to join the big band
summary: After a battle of the bands with Harlan Leonard, Bird gave notice and joined McShann's big band, where he rehearsed the reed section.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And we had a battle of the bands with Harlan Leonard one night -- was it a battle? Yeah.
Was this with your small band or --

See, and the big band, you know, and they can't be very old, and so Bird come up after we got through and said, 'Man, I want to play with you cats.' I said, 'Well, man, you know, you're with Harlan. You know Harlan ain't about to let you go.' He said, 'Well, man, I'll leave the band.' I said, 'Well, you got to give them some kind of notice or something.' He said, 'Well, okay, I'll give notice. I'll give him two week notice -- I'll give him a week.' I said, 'Give him two weeks' notice and take your time and come on in the band.' He said, 'Okay.' So he gave Harlan notice and come on with the big band, you know.

Now, during that time, see, that's the reason I say he had broke his habit, because he would take the reed, see, and I'd as point him, you know, to rehearse the reed section, because we would have section rehearsals. The brass would be over here rehearsing. The reeds would be over here. Bones over there, rhythm section over here, different parts of the hall, you know, whatever, you know. And then we'd bring the whole thing together, you know. And Bird used to keep right on and he'd keep right on them cats, you know.
He was really conscientious about it then?
He was conscientious about it. See, now, I never was worried about the reeds because I knew what Bird was going to do with them, you know.
